aiKnowledge.intro: Governs the global AI Chat assistant: a master switch plus four knowledge sources. Takes effect immediately (hot-reload). Requires Llm:Enabled.
aiKnowledge.operationalHint: Provides the secret-redacted workflow definition, static workflow analysis, and computed cron fire times. Pure listings (which workflows exist, recent/failed executions, managed machines) are answered through the database source (text2sql, global Admin only) — no separate source needed for those.
aiKnowledge.sourceCodeWarning: Warning: the full git-tracked source tree (incl. deploy/, scripts/, tests/) ships with the install and becomes queryable by Admin/Operator.
aiKnowledge.dbWarning: Warning: the chat can run read-only SQL (text2sql) against the NodePilot app DB. Writes are rejected server-side; secret columns are hidden in the schema view and redacted (***) in results. Only global Admins can invoke these tools; folder grants never elevate an Operator.
aiKnowledge.rootsHint: Empty = default next to the app (knowledge/docs and knowledge/source). In dev, point at the repo for live editing.

hotReloadHint: Changes apply immediately — no service restart required.

dbAdmin.title: SQL Query Console
dbAdmin.writeWarning: Enabled: Admins can mutate the database from the query editor. Per-statement confirmation still required.
dbAdmin.maxRowsHint: Hard cap to prevent OOM on accidental SELECT *. Default 10,000.
dbAdmin.confirmEnableBody: This lets any Admin run UPDATE/DELETE/DROP statements via the SQL console — bypassing every per-table guard (masked columns, last-admin protection). Type the confirmation phrase to proceed.

restartBannerBody: The following settings have been saved but will only take effect after a service restart:
envBadgeTooltip: This value is overridden by the environment variable {{key}}. A UI save will be persisted, but the environment variable continues to win.
cliBadgeTooltip: This value is overridden by a command-line argument.
etagConflictBody: This section was modified since you loaded it (other browser tab, other admin). Choose how to proceed:
validationErrorsTitle: These values would prevent the next service start:
smtpEnableSslWarning: Warning: a username is configured but TLS is disabled. SMTP credentials and message bodies will travel in plaintext. Only recommended for local, non-public relays.

perf.modeExplainer: With automatic sizing NodePilot derives the values below from the detected CPU and memory. Switch on manual tuning to use the configured values instead — they stay stored either way.
perf.modePendingRestart: The saved mode differs from the one this process booted in. The runspace pool and dispatch worker pool are sized once at startup, so a restart is required.
perf.inertUnderAuto: Automatic sizing is active — these values are stored but not in force.
perf.manualPendingRestart: Manual tuning is selected but not in force yet — the automatically derived values govern until the service restarts.
perf.autoPendingRestart: Automatic sizing is selected but not in force yet — the configured values govern until the service restarts.
perf.safetyCapHint: Safety cap against runaway trigger loops and sub-workflow cascades — not a throughput setting. Always applies, in both sizing modes.

sec.blockPrivateNetworksHint: Stops the restApi activity from reaching targets in private networks (RFC1918) or on loopback — the baseline SSRF guard once target URLs can come from workflow parameters or trigger payloads. Exceptions go through the allow-list below and nowhere else. Link-local and cloud metadata (169.254.…) stay blocked even with this switch off.
sec.outboundAllowedHostsHint: Exception to "block private networks" for restApi targets and redirects. Enter exact hosts or IPs only. Link-local/cloud metadata can never be allowed. Wait for Condition network probes have their own list — see the card below.
sec.probeAllowedHostsHint: These probes run through PowerShell and cannot re-validate the destination at connect time, so they admit only exactly listed hosts — an empty list rejects every probe. Deliberately separate from the outbound allow-list above: permitting "check my own service" must not also open restApi to loopback. Matching is exact; "127.0.0.1" does not cover "localhost". This list alone decides — the outbound allow-list above is not consulted for probes. Link-local/cloud-metadata (169.254.…) stays blocked regardless.
sec.restApiProxyEnabledHint: Routes outbound calls from the restApi activity through the proxy configured below. Overridable per node via the proxyMode key. Applies to restApi only — LLM calls have their own proxy block under Integrations, and WinRM and SMTP never use this proxy.
sec.rejectTraversalHint: Rejects any path containing '..' in every path-bearing activity (fileOperation, folderOperation, textFileEdit, fileHash, zipOperation). Off means a workflow can climb out of an allowed root — a path from a trigger payload is enough. UNC paths and wildcards are always rejected regardless of this switch.
sec.allowedRootsHint: While this list has entries, every path must resolve inside one of these directories after symlinks/junctions are followed. An empty list means this list imposes no limit — only the service account's own permissions then decide where a workflow can write. The check runs on the NodePilot host; for WinRM targets the target system's ACLs remain the authoritative boundary.
sec.requireConnectionRef: Require named connectionRef (block inline connection strings)
sec.requireConnectionRefHint: The sql activity then accepts only a named connectionRef from SqlActivity:ConnectionStrings. A connectionString stored in the node is rejected, as are individual fields (server/user/password) carrying credentials; integrated auth and file-based SQLite without a password stay allowed. The point: no database secrets in the workflow definition, where they escape rotation and audit.
sec.disallowShellExecuteHint: Rejects useShellExecute=true in the startProgram activity. Going through the shell lets Windows launch the target by file association — documents, scripts and URLs included — and the shell parser is a second injection surface on top of PowerShell quoting. Only turn this off when a workflow demonstrably needs shell-mediated launches.
sec.requireWebhookSecretHint: A webhookTrigger without a configured secret will not fire. Verification follows the trigger's signatureMode — either the X-Webhook-Secret header or an HMAC signature; HMAC mode is always fail-closed regardless of this switch. Off means anyone who knows the webhook URL can start the workflow — every secret-less hit is additionally logged as a warning.
sec.externalTriggerHint: Legacy key for <0>POST /api/trigger/...</0>. It can start only explicitly listed workflows that contain an enabled Manual/API trigger. New integrations should use hashed, scoped key entries in configuration.
sec.externalTriggerAllowedWorkflowIdsHint: Empty means deny all. Use immutable workflow GUIDs, one entry per workflow; names and wildcards are not accepted.
sec.strictAllowedHostsHint: Aborts service start-up when AllowedHosts is unsafely wide: '*', empty, or a deployment-template placeholder that was never substituted. It applies at boot only, never at runtime — a change here takes effect on the next start. Without this switch, a wide-open list is only a warning in the log.
sec.allowedHostsFieldHint: Host headers the host filter accepts — semicolon-separated, ideally concrete FQDNs. Include 'localhost': the installers' own health probe targets https://localhost:<port>/healthz/ready and would otherwise be rejected with a 400.
sec.remoteNote: <0>Remote (WinRM):</0> RequireWinRmSsl, WinRM timeouts and the session pool are edited under <1>Performance → Remote</1> — every remote switch lives there together, so one save overwrites the whole block atomically.
sec.reencryptHint: Re-encrypts every credential password, secret-flagged global variable, and encrypted workflow-history definition with the active secret provider. Run this after rotating the master key or switching Secrets:Provider (keep the legacy provider configured for the migration window, see docs/secrets-providers.md).
sec.reencryptConfirm: Re-encrypt all stored secrets with the active provider now?
sec.reencryptDone: Re-encrypted {{credentials}} credential(s), {{globals}} global secret(s), and {{workflowVersions}} workflow history version(s).
sec.reencryptPartial: Partial success: {{rewritten}} re-encrypted, {{skipped}} skipped — review the affected entries below before removing the legacy provider.
sec.reencryptResultPartial: Rotation completed with entries that still need attention

auth.allowedGroupsRequired: At least one allowed group SID is required before LDAP can be enabled.
auth.ldapHealthHint: Tests TLS trust, service bind, search base and group resolution with the current draft.
auth.ntlmDisabledByPolicy: NTLM is disabled by host/domain policy
auth.ntlmPolicyRequired: Confirm and enforce the NTLM policy before enabling Windows SSO.
auth.localLoginHint: Break-glass mode only permits explicitly designated emergency accounts and audits every use.
auth.oidcHint: Authorization Code flow with PKCE. Issuer, client and claim settings become active after restart.
auth.oidcGroupsRequired: At least one allowed OIDC group is required before OIDC can be enabled.
auth.oidcNoMappings: No OIDC role mappings — users default to Viewer.
auth.scimHint: Provision and revoke OIDC users and groups from your identity provider. Use a dedicated random token with at least 32 characters.
auth.noMappings: No mappings — users default to <0>Viewer</0> role unless explicitly granted.

integrations.enableToolCallingHint: Lets the workflow chat assistant call read-only analysis tools. Requires a model with reliable function-calling.
integrations.baseUrlHint: e.g. https://api.openai.com/v1 — a URL ending in /responses uses the OpenAI Responses API; one ending in /chat/completions is used verbatim.
integrations.activeProfileHint: Every AI feature uses this profile.
integrations.profileNotDeletable: Defined in "{{source}}" — editable here, but it can only be removed in that configuration source.
integrations.noProfiles: No LLM profile yet. Add one and select it to use the AI features.
integrations.activeProfileRequired: Select an active profile, or turn the LLM integration off.
integrations.proxyModeHint: Applies to every AI call — chat, generation, and the llmQuery activity. Changes take effect immediately; save first, then use the Test button.
integrations.proxyModeSystemHint: Uses the proxy configured for the account the NodePilot service runs under (Windows: WinHTTP/WinINET), including its own bypass rules. Changes to the Windows settings take effect after a service restart.
integrations.proxyBypassListHint: Hosts reached directly. Wildcards allowed, e.g. localhost or *.corp.local — this is how a local Ollama keeps working alongside a proxy.
integrations.proxyUseDefaultCredentials: Use the service account's Windows credentials
integrations.proxyUseDefaultCredentialsHint: For domain-integrated proxies using NTLM/Kerberos. Replaces username and password.

systemInfo.bootstrapNote: These values are bootstrap-only and read from <0>appsettings.json</0>, environment variables, or the secrets provider. They cannot be changed through the UI — modify them in your deployment configuration and restart the service.
